context: A uni student interviews a retired diplomat about embassy life
purpose: Teach: 大使/大使館/通訳/フランス語/演習/妄想/スパイ/匿名

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 本日はお時間ありがとうございます。卒論で外交官のお仕事を扱っていて、大使館での日常を伺いたいんです。
lines.en: Thank you for your time today. My thesis covers diplomats' work, so I'd like to ask about daily life at the embassy.
lines.style: Polite, slightly nervous student opening an interview with respectful framing.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ああ、構わんよ。私はパリの大使館に長くいてね、フランス語の通訳も兼ねていた時期があった。
lines.en: Ah, not at all. I was at the Paris embassy for a long time, and there was a period I also doubled as a French interpreter.
lines.style: Warm, reminiscent elder tone with measured, old-fashioned cadence.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 通訳まで！大使ご本人の隣で訳すというのは、相当な緊張感ですよね。
lines.en: Even interpreting! Translating right next to the ambassador himself must come with enormous pressure.
lines.style: Genuinely impressed, curious student leaning forward in conversation.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: そりゃもう、毎朝が演習みたいなものでね。一語間違えれば国の立場が変わる、と上司に脅されたよ。
lines.en: Oh absolutely, every morning was like a drill. My boss threatened that one wrong word could shift the nation's position.
lines.style: Dry humor with a chuckle, recalling old workplace pressure fondly.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: ネットだと「外交官は全員スパイだ」みたいな匿名の書き込みも多いんですが、実際どうでしたか？
lines.en: Online there are lots of anonymous posts claiming "all diplomats are spies" — what was the reality?
lines.style: Cheeky probing question, half-joking but genuinely curious about misconceptions.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ははは、それは大半が妄想だな。情報は集めるが、映画みたいな話じゃない。書類とお茶と握手の繰り返しだよ。
lines.en: Hahaha, most of that is fantasy. We gather information, sure, but it's nothing like the movies. Just paperwork, tea, and handshakes on repeat.
lines.style: Hearty laugh, gently dismissive elder correcting a young person's assumptions.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: なるほど、地道なんですね。最後に、これから外交を目指す学生に一言いただけますか？
lines.en: I see, so it's steady work. Lastly, could you give one piece of advice to students aiming for diplomacy?
lines.style: Respectful wrap-up tone, inviting a final piece of wisdom.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 語学を一つ、本気で磨きなさい。フランス語でも何でもいい。言葉が信頼を作るんだ。
lines.en: Master one language seriously. French, or anything else. Words are what build trust.
lines.style: Solemn, fatherly closing advice delivered with quiet conviction.
